Research.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
Research.summary: SWE-Duel proposes a benchmark where two coding agents generate tasks and oracles for each other at evaluation time, preventing training data leakage and benchmark saturation. This adversarial self-scaling approach is practically important for teams evaluating coding agents, as it keeps difficulty pegged to agent capability rather than a fixed release. Builders of AI coding pipelines should track this as it addresses a core reliability problem with static benchmarks.

Research.title: Contextual Correction of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
Research.summary: This paper improves speculative decoding by using diffusion-based drafters that propose multiple tokens in parallel, then applying a contextual correction step to improve acceptance rates. The approach can meaningfully accelerate inference for large models without sacrificing output quality, which is directly relevant for teams optimizing LLM serving costs. Practitioners running high-throughput inference pipelines should evaluate this as a drop-in acceleration technique.

Research.title: GeopoliticalQA: Benchmarking Retrieval and Generation over Intelligence Reports
Research.summary: GeopoliticalQA introduces a benchmark of 5,525 QA pairs grounded in 415 open-source geopolitical intelligence reports, targeting RAG systems operating on complex, heterogeneous expert documents. This fills a gap for teams building retrieval pipelines for high-stakes analytical domains where documents have dense cross-references and nuanced reasoning requirements. It provides a useful evaluation target for enterprise RAG products targeting government, defense, or policy use cases.

Research.title: Reflective Prompt Optimization of a Deep-Research Agent: Measuring Transferable Gains and Prompt-Level Overfitting
Research.summary: This paper identifies a critical failure mode in prompt optimization for factual agent tasks: an optimizer with access to training examples can embed answers directly into the prompt, producing illusory in-distribution gains that don't transfer. The authors propose a topic-disjoint, multi-seed evaluation protocol to distinguish genuine prompt improvements from memorization. This is a must-read for teams using automated prompt optimization tools on knowledge-intensive or research agents.

Tools.title: perturber: A Stateless Service for Semantics-Preserving Text Perturbations
Tools.summary: perturber is an open-source, stateless microservice from IBM Research that applies meaning-preserving text perturbations (e.g., typos, paraphrases) to benchmark inputs in a reproducible, benchmark-agnostic way. It addresses the well-known gap between clean benchmark performance and real-world robustness, letting teams stress-test models against noisy inputs without coupling perturbation logic to their eval framework. Useful for any team running LLM evaluations who wants to get a more realistic picture of production performance.

Tools.title: Impactful Scheduling for GPU Clusters
Tools.summary: AllenAI's blog post on their GPU cluster scheduling approach details techniques for maximizing research throughput and minimizing wasted compute on large shared infrastructure. The post offers concrete lessons for ML platform teams managing multi-tenant GPU clusters, particularly around job prioritization and preemption policies. Relevant for any organization running or scaling its own training infrastructure.

Industry News.title: OpenAI Expands GPT-6.1 Sol Context to 500k Tokens, Drops Long-Context Fees for Subscribers
Industry News.summary: OpenAI has increased the default context window for GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex and Work from 272k to 500k tokens (~80% increase), reducing the frequency of context compactions on long agentic tasks. Crucially, long-context fees are waived for subscription users, lowering the cost barrier for developers building agents that need to maintain extensive state over time. This is a significant practical improvement for anyone building deep-research or long-horizon coding agents on the OpenAI platform.

Industry News.title: Research Firm Calls Anthropic's IPO 'Unprecedented Test of Investor Gullibility'
Industry News.summary: A research firm has publicly questioned the valuation basis of Anthropic's anticipated IPO, framing it as a stress test of how much speculative premium public markets will assign to frontier AI labs. The skepticism centers on the gap between current revenue and the multi-billion dollar valuations, a dynamic relevant to how enterprise buyers and investors think about AI vendor stability. AI product builders dependent on Anthropic's APIs should monitor this as it may affect future pricing and service continuity.

Industry News.title: QGIS Bans AI-Assisted Contributions
Industry News.summary: The QGIS open-source GIS project has voted to ban AI-assisted code contributions via an official enhancement proposal, citing concerns about code quality, license compliance, and contributor accountability. This is one of the more prominent open-source projects to formalize such a ban, and it signals a broader tension that AI product builders relying on open-source dependencies may need to navigate. Teams contributing to open-source projects as part of their AI strategy should be aware that community norms around AI-generated code are hardening.

Industry News.title: Building AI for Reliable Execution: Lessons from Industrial Robotics (Standard Bots)
Industry News.summary: Standard Bots describes their AI stack for factory automation, where pretrained models learn manipulation tasks from human demonstrations and improve iteratively from real deployment corrections. The episode surfaces hard-won lessons about the gap between lab reliability and production reliability in physical AI systems. Relevant for teams building AI in safety-critical or high-stakes execution environments beyond pure software agents.

Industry News.title: TypeSafe/Jev Hits $100M ARR and $7.5B Valuation Three Weeks After Launch
Industry News.summary: The AI coding and developer tooling startup TypeSafe/Jev reportedly crossed $100M ARR and a $7.5B valuation within weeks of launch, an extraordinary growth trajectory even by AI standards. This signals continued explosive investor and enterprise appetite for AI developer tools despite broader market skepticism. Competitors and adjacent product builders in the AI dev tools space should treat this as a key market signal about where enterprise spending is concentrating.
